name: Indonesia
shortSummary: India and Indonesia, the world's two largest democracies in their respective regions, maintain a Strategic Partnership with growing maritime cooperation, though trade remains heavily weighted toward Indonesian coal and palm oil exports.

majorAreasOfCooperation.description: Access to Sabang port supports Indian Ocean surveillance near the Malacca Strait.
Indonesia is a major supplier of thermal coal to Indian power plants.

majorChallenges.title: Trade imbalance
majorChallenges.description: India runs a substantial deficit driven by coal and palm oil imports.

recentDevelopments.title: Continued Comprehensive Strategic Partnership implementation
recentDevelopments.description: India and Indonesia continued defence and maritime cooperation under their 2018 Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including use of Sabang port access.
recentDevelopments.whyItMatters: Steady progress in a relationship central to India's Indo-Pacific maritime strategy.

historicalEvents.title: Treaty of Friendship
historicalEvents.description: India and Indonesia sign a treaty of friendship shortly after both gaining independence.

historicalEvents.title: Strategic Partnership
historicalEvents.description: India and Indonesia elevate ties to a Strategic Partnership.

historicalEvents.title: Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and Sabang Port Access
historicalEvents.description: Ties are further elevated, and Indonesia grants India access to the strategically located Sabang port near the Malacca Strait.

agreements.name: Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
agreements.description: Framework covering defence, maritime, trade and connectivity cooperation.

defenceCooperation.name: Garuda Shakti
defenceCooperation.description: Bilateral special forces exercise between India and Indonesia.

multilateralRelations.detail: Engaged through India's Act East Policy.
Joint member; Indonesia hosted the G20 in 2022, India in 2023.
Joint member on Indian Ocean maritime cooperation.
